title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in B-flat major
hook: Brahms called it “a very small piano concerto”; it has four movements and lasts almost an hour.

painting.title: March Mood: Early Spring in the Vienna Woods
painting.pairingNote: Early spring in the Vienna Woods, where Brahms finished the concerto at Pressbaum in 1881, painted three years later.

facts: Brahms began the concerto in 1878 and finished it in the summer of 1881 at Pressbaum, near Vienna, shortly after returning from a journey to Italy. It came 22 years after his First Piano Concerto.

He played the solo part himself at the premiere in Budapest on 9 November 1881. It was an immediate success, and he went on to perform it in many cities. He dedicated it to his old teacher, Eduard Marxsen.

Brahms liked to understate. He told a friend he had written “a very small piano concerto with a very small and pretty scherzo”. In fact it has four movements instead of the usual three and lasts about 50 minutes.
Piano and orchestra work together more than they compete. The piano is fiendishly hard, but it often accompanies, and in the slow movement the main melody belongs to a solo cello.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a broad, noble opening that grows into a storm (I), a fierce [[scherzo|scherzo]] (II), a cello song and a still, hushed dream (III), a light, graceful dance (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro non troppo
movements.summary: A solo horn opens the concerto with a calm call, and the piano answers. Almost at once the piano breaks into a loud solo passage, and only then does the orchestra start its own presentation of the themes. The movement is a concerto [[sonata-form|sonata form]] on a very large scale, with long stretches of struggle before the horn’s peace returns.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, the horn call
mainIdeas.description: a calm, rising phrase that ends with a gentle turn.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a sad, expressive melody in the violins, in a minor key.

notice: The horn call comes back at every turning point: at the start, at the beginning of the development and at the recapitulation. Each time the piano’s answer is different.
In the first minute the piano plays its cadenza before the orchestra has properly begun. Brahms turns the usual order of a concerto upside down.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Gilels recorded both Brahms concertos with Jochum in Berlin in June 1972. On the Spotify album this concerto is tracks 4–7, after the First Concerto.

movements.heading: Allegro appassionato
movements.summary: The “very small and pretty scherzo” is a storm. The piano drives a fierce theme in D minor, and a sweeping string melody answers it. In the middle the music turns to a bright D major and a striding, march-like tune that the piano and orchestra finally shout together.

mainIdeas.name: The storm
mainIdeas.description: a driving, restless theme for the piano, beginning on a strong upbeat.

mainIdeas.name: The yearning tune
mainIdeas.description: a sweeping melody for violins and violas in unison.
The [[trio|trio]] tune: a bright, striding melody in D major.

stops.hear: The piano launches a stormy, driving theme, and the orchestra answers
Violins and violas in unison play a sweeping, yearning melody
The stormy opening again
The theme is broken up and tossed between piano and orchestra
Bright D major: the violins play a strong, striding tune
The piano alone with a quiet new idea, then soft, wandering lines
stops.happening: A calm moment before the climax

stops.hear: The striding tune at full force, piano and orchestra together
The stormy theme returns, changed and shorter

stops.label: Last 25 seconds
stops.hear: Massive surges on the piano and loud closing chords
stops.happening: The movement ends in D major

notice: This is the last movement with trumpets and timpani. After it, Brahms leaves them out of the concerto altogether.

movements.heading: Andante
movements.summary: The slow movement opens with a song for solo cello, not for piano. When the piano finally enters, it seems to improvise around the melody. A stormy passage breaks out and passes, and in the middle the music almost stops in a hushed, distant key. Then the cello returns with the song.

mainIdeas.name: The cello song
mainIdeas.description: a long, slow, tender melody. Brahms later turned it into a song, *Immer leiser wird mein Schlummer* (“My slumber grows ever lighter”).

mainIdeas.name: The dream
mainIdeas.description: a hushed melody for two clarinets over the piano’s sparse chords, in F-sharp major.

stops.hear: A solo cello sings a long, slow melody over soft strings and bassoons
The oboe joins the cello as the melody closes
stops.happening: The end of the opening section

stops.hear: The piano enters quietly with wide, winding arpeggios, then dreams on alone
stops.happening: The piano’s first entry, almost a [[cadenza|cadenza]]

stops.hear: The orchestra bursts in with the main theme in a minor key; the piano surges against it
stops.happening: A stormy passage in B-flat minor

stops.hear: The storm subsides; violins and violas hold quiet chords
Very slow and still: two clarinets play a simple, hushed melody over the piano’s sparse chords
stops.happening: *Più adagio*, in F-sharp major, the heart of the movement

stops.hear: The solo cello returns with the song
The piano plays soft, floating figures, then a long trill

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: Cello and orchestra end quietly in B-flat major

notice: In the *Più adagio* the clarinets and piano play so quietly and so slowly that time seems to stop. It is the furthest point of the concerto, in key and in mood, from the horn call that opened it.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: The cello solo is played by Ottomar Borwitzky.

movements.heading: Allegretto grazioso
movements.summary: After all the drama, a light, smiling [[rondo|rondo]]. The piano’s graceful tune keeps returning between episodes, one of them a sad melody with a Hungarian lilt. At the end the tempo quickens and the tune skips into a new rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: The rondo tune
mainIdeas.description: a light, graceful melody for piano over plucked strings.

mainIdeas.name: The Hungarian tune
mainIdeas.description: a swaying, melancholy melody in A minor, shared between woodwinds and strings.

The piano alone plays a playful answering phrase

stops.hear: Sweeping piano arpeggios and bright closing chords

notice: In the faster coda, listen to the rondo tune turned into a skipping triple rhythm. It is the same melody, but it suddenly sounds like a march.

threads.title: Partners
threads.body: The horn opens the concerto, a cello sings the slow movement, and the piano often accompanies. This is a concerto for piano and orchestra together, almost a symphony with piano.

threads.title: From struggle to ease
threads.body: Two big, stormy movements are followed by a song and a dance. The weight of the concerto lies in its first half; the second half relaxes.

threads.title: Understatement
threads.body: Brahms called it very small. It is one of the longest and hardest concertos in the repertoire.
